info.title: tavrn Node API
info.description: API of a tavrn node. Clients, bots and other nodes use the same routes. Errors follow RFC 9457 (Problem Details).

get.summary: Discovery document. Read by clients and other nodes; cacheable for 5 minutes.
Progress of an account deletion (the token comes with the deletion's answer).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token of the confirmation mail.

get.summary: Preview of an account invite (public): valid or not.
Account deletions (the undo is possible while `state` is processing or done and `purge_after` lies ahead).
The applications of this node (node admins).
The node's application blocklist (node admins).

post.summary:
Block a bot on this node: it is uninstalled from every room here (`reason: blocked`) and refused for
installations, tokens and federated logins (`403 app.blocked`).

delete.summary: Lift a block (no automatic reinstallation).

get.summary: Command definitions of the applications known on this node and their approval state (node admins).

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: `pending`, `approved` or `rejected`; all without.

get.summary: Whether this node requires the approval of application commands (node admins; for the admin UI).

post.summary: Approve command definitions by their hash (node admins).
Reject command definitions by their hash (node admins): they stay out of the palettes.

delete.summary: Delete an application (node admins, APPLICATIONS.md §1.7).

patch.summary:
Disable or re-enable an application (node admins). Disabling closes the bot's WebSockets and ends its
federated sessions; tokens then fail with `403 app.disabled`.

get.summary: Node-wide audit log (registrations, admin actions).
Node-wide bans.

post.summary: Node-wide ban for `user@domain` or an entire domain.

delete.summary: Lift a node-wide ban (a local account is not automatically re-enabled).

get.summary: Delisted nodes and rooms (node admins).

delete.summary: Delists a node (§7.4): it is neither shown nor passed on, also after new announces. Audited.

post.summary: Undoes a delisting. The node reappears with its next announce or refresh. Audited.

get.summary: Reported nodes with their report counts, most recently reported first (node admins).
The reports about one node, newest first (at most 200, node admins).

delete.summary: Dismisses (deletes) the reports about one node. Audited.
Delists one room (also one of this node's own rooms). Audited.

get.summary: Effective values for a user and/or a room (room keys are evaluated for the room's owner).

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User id or address (local users only).

parameters.name: room
parameters.description: Room id.

get.summary: Grants, optionally of one subject, ordered by id and paged with `after`.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: `user:<id or address>` or `room:<id>`.

parameters.name: include_expired
parameters.description: Include expired grants (kept for a week).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 100, at most 500).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Grant id to continue after.

post.summary: Grant a plan and/or overrides to a local user or a room.

delete.summary: Delete a grant.

patch.summary: Change a grant's plan, overrides, expiry or note (the subject stays).

get.summary: The known entitlement keys with their rules and node defaults.
All plans, by name.

post.summary: Create a plan.

delete.summary: Delete a plan that no grant uses (`409 entitlements.plan_in_use` otherwise).

patch.summary: Rename a plan or replace its limits (every grant using it changes with it).

get.summary: Peers this node knows (fetched their discovery document, checked or blocked them), by domain.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1–200, default 100.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Domain of the last entry of the previous page.

post.summary:
Blocks a peer by hand (`status = blocked`): no federation with it in either direction, its users'
federated sessions end. Stays until an admin unblocks it. Audited.

Runs the conformance checks against a peer now (forced) and returns its state. Consequences apply as
for automatic runs: a hard failure blocks the peer, a clean run lifts an automatic block. Audited.

Lifts a manual or automatic block or a key conflict (the keys the peer publishes now are accepted on
the next fetch). Audited.

get.summary: List account invites.

post.summary: Create an account invite (for `TAVRN_REGISTRATION=invite`).

delete.summary: Delete an account invite.

get.summary: The designated contact for notices.

put.summary: Set the designated contact (shown in `GET /node` and on the notice form).

get.summary: The published documents (with Markdown) for the editor.

put.summary: Publish a new version of a document (every publish of the terms asks existing users again).

delete.summary: Unpublish a document (its versions stay in the history).

get.summary: Cases, newest first, with filters.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only this state.

parameters.name: basis
parameters.description: Only this legal basis.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text in the reporter's name or e-mail, the work, the target address or the case id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (1–200, default 50).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Cases older than this case id (pagination, newest first).

get.summary: Every kept case with its trail and counter-notices (JSON archive for the operator's records).
A case with its trail, counter-notices, the reported content (plaintext only) and the repeat counter.

post.summary: Act on a case: remove content, disable the account, reject, forward to the content's node, or set the state.
Decide on the uploader's counter-notice.

get.summary: A non-binding template for the editor ("Insert template"): not legal advice.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: `en` or `de` (privacy policy); the imprint template is German, the terms skeleton English.

delete.summary:
Purge the cached copies of another node's emoji or clip (node admins, abuse cases). The origin's
own deletion never reaches cached copies.

get.summary: Overview for node admins: counts and effective configuration.
Every report of the node, newest first (node admins).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open`, `resolved` or `dismissed` (default: all).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Admin list only: `room` or `node`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1–100, default 50.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A report id: older reports only (paging).

get.summary: The node's rooms with their roles (node admins).
get.description: For pickers such as the single sign-on group map, which names rooms and roles by id.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the room name.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1–100, default 50.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A room id: rooms after it (paging).

get.summary: The group → rights map in force (§8.5).

put.summary: Replaces the group map (unless the environment fixes it). Takes effect at the users' next SSO login.

get.summary: Admin API tokens (never their secrets).

post.summary: Create an admin API token (session only: tokens cannot create tokens). The secret is returned once.

delete.summary: Revoke (delete) an admin API token.

get.summary: Search and list local users.

patch.summary: Disable/enable a user, set the admin permission, grant room creation.

put.summary:
Correct a local user's date of birth on request (PROTOCOL.md §5e: users set it once). Audited as
`admin.date_of_birth` without the date itself. The minimum age is not applied here: an account the operator
finds too young is disabled or deleted instead.

post.summary: Delete a user's account on the user's request (reauth token, the username as confirmation; audited).

get.summary: Export a user's data on the user's request (needs the admin's reauth token; audited).

post.summary: Permanently delete all messages and files of a user on this node (preview, then confirmation).

Rescue for a locked-out user: removes TOTP, all WebAuthn credentials (with their passkey secret
storage entries) and the recovery codes, and signs the user out everywhere. The next login lands
in `enrollment_required`; the `recovery` secret storage entry stays, so history is unaffected.
Admins cannot reset their own factors here.
Undo a deletion within the grace period.

get.summary: The caller's applications.

post.summary: Create an application with its bot account (APPLICATIONS.md §1.3).

get.summary: The bot's own application (with an app token).
The bot's own command set (app token with the `commands` scope).

put.summary: Replace the bot's own command set (app token with the `commands` scope, 10 per hour).

get.summary:
With an app token: every room the bot is installed in, on this node and on others (the SDK opens
federated sessions with those nodes).

post.summary:
Rotate the calling token (once per 24 hours): same token row and device, new secret with the same
lifetime; the previous secret stays valid for 24 hours so a bot can restart with the new one.

get.summary: Transfers of applications offered to the caller (accept or decline them).
One of the caller's applications.

delete.summary: Delete an application (§1.7): tokens, devices and memberships go; the bot stays as a tombstone.

patch.summary: Change an application (owner).

put.summary: Set the bot's avatar (raw body, media pipeline of PROTOCOL.md §6b, 256 × 256 avatar rules).

delete.summary: Remove the bot's avatar.

get.summary: The command set of one of the caller's applications (owner).

put.summary: Replace the whole command set of one of the caller's applications (owner, 10 per hour).

post.summary:
Reset the bot's identity (lost or leaked key file): its identity key, device attestations, KeyPackages
and backups are deleted; the bot process sets a new key on its next start.

get.summary:
The public document of an application (no authentication, CORS-open, cacheable 5 minutes). Disabled,
blocked and deleted applications answer `404 app.not_found`.
The application's event subscription (owner).

put.summary: Set (or replace) the subscription after verifying the URL with a ping (§6.3).

delete.summary: Remove the subscription and every queued event.

post.summary: Re-enable a disabled (or failing) subscription; the URL is verified again.

get.summary: The application's tokens (never their secrets).

post.summary: Create a token, i.e. a bot device (`409 app.token_limit` beyond 5). The secret is shown once.

delete.summary: Revoke a token: the token and its device are deleted (`devices.changed`, `mls.remove_needed`).

post.summary: Reset a token: same device, new secret; the old secret is invalid at once and open WebSockets close.
Offer the application to another local user (pending for 7 days, one at a time).

delete.summary: Cancel the pending transfer (owner).

post.summary:
Accept a transfer: the application becomes the caller's; every token and device of the bot is revoked
and its identity reset, so the new owner starts with fresh credentials.
Decline a transfer offered to the caller.

One-time code for the web client of another node or a native app (connect flow, FEDERATION.md §8). Needs a full
session of a local user and, because the code becomes a new session, a reauth token (`Tavrn-Reauth`, PROTOCOL.md
§5c; not for an `unlock` session); remote users get `federation.local_only`. With `origin` the page redirects the code to
that web client; with `session_id` the node keeps it, and the optional `sealed_unlock`, for the app's next poll of
its app session. An `unlock` session issues no code: its own user sends `sealed_unlock` and gets `204`.

204.description: Unlock session: the sealed unlock material waits for the app's poll

post.summary:
Creates an app session of the connect flow (FEDERATION.md §8 step 3, `connect.app`) for a native app without an
https origin. No authentication for a sign-in; an `unlock` session needs the app's full session of a local user and
belongs to that user. Rate-limited per client IP and for the whole node.

get.summary:
Polls an app session (FEDERATION.md §8 step 3): `pending` until the user confirmed on the node's page, then
`ready` with the one-time code and the sealed unlock material exactly once, then `410 connect.session_expired`.
No authentication: the code is useless without the app's PKCE verifier, the sealed material without the app's
key. Rate-limited per session and per client IP.

post.summary:
Exchanges a connect code for a session (FEDERATION.md §8): of a new device, or of the device the request
proves to hold (`device`, ENCRYPTION.md §3.4). No authentication: the code, the PKCE verifier and the request's
`Origin` (must equal the bound origin) prove it. Every failure is `connect.code_invalid`, and the code is spent by
the first attempt; a refused device proof only means a new device.

A single-use login nonce for a device proof (PROTOCOL.md §5b, ENCRYPTION.md §3.4): the client signs it with the
key of a device it still holds and sends `device` with the login, so the new session continues that device.

get.summary: The account's second factors.

post.summary:
Federated login of a user of another node (FEDERATION.md §2.5). No password, captcha or second
factor here: the home node enforced them before issuing the token.

Request a password reset by email. Always answers 204, so no accounts can be guessed. At most three mails per
account and hour; a link that has not expired stays valid (a new request sends no new one). A node without
SMTP answers `503 mail.unavailable` (development nodes log the mail instead).

Login with username and password. Returns a pre-auth token: `second_factor_required`
(verify a factor) or `enrollment_required` (the account has no factor yet). The session for the
new device follows the second factor.

Log out: revoke all sessions of this device. An SSO session answers `200` with the provider's
logout URL when the provider has one (APPLICATIONS.md §8.6), otherwise `204`.

parameters.name: forget_device
parameters.description:
The client deleted this device's keys: the device is removed as well (like a deletion in the device list:
`mls.remove_needed`, pending removals of its leaves, `devices.changed`). Local accounts only.

get.summary: The provider identity linked to the account, or null.

delete.summary:
Unlinks the identity; only if the account keeps a password and a second factor (§8.3). Needs a reauth token
(`Tavrn-Reauth`, PROTOCOL.md §5c).

post.summary:
Starts an SSO flow (§8.2). `login` needs no session; `link` and `reauth` need the full session of a
local user (`link`: not linked yet, and a reauth token in `Tavrn-Reauth`, PROTOCOL.md §5c; `reauth`: linked).

Exchanges the one-time code (single use, 60 s, bound to the start request's challenge). The login is
completed here: the account is found or provisioned, the group map applied and the session issued
without a second factor (§8.4). `link` and `reauth` additionally need the session that started the flow.

Re-authentication (PROTOCOL.md §5c): the password or a WebAuthn assertion yields a reauth token for this session,
valid for five minutes. SSO accounts use the provider's `reauth` flow (`POST /auth/oidc/token`).
Starts a WebAuthn assertion for a re-authentication (any of the account's passkeys or security keys).
New recovery codes (the old set becomes invalid). Needs the password or a reauth token.

New access token; the refresh token is rotated. Parallel refreshes with the same token, and the previous token
within 30 seconds of its rotation, get the same new pair; an older reuse revokes the session (PROTOCOL.md §5b).

Create an account: open, by invite or closed, depending on the node setting. The answer is
a pre-auth token in stage `enroll`: the account becomes usable once a second factor is enrolled.
Set the password with the token received by email; all sessions are signed out.
Completes a password login with a TOTP code or a recovery code; returns the session.

delete.summary:
Removes TOTP. Needs the password, or a reauth token (PROTOCOL.md §5c) together with a current code; refused if it
is the last factor.

post.summary: Activates the enrolled TOTP with a current code.

Starts a TOTP enrollment (session or pre-auth token in stage `enroll`). Replaces an
unconfirmed enrollment; a confirmed TOTP must be removed first.
Verify the email address with the token received by email.

get.summary: The account's WebAuthn credentials.

delete.summary: Removes a credential and its secret storage entry; refused if it is the last factor.

post.summary: Completes a WebAuthn assertion and returns the session.
Starts a WebAuthn assertion (second factor or passkey-only login).
Completes the registration; with a pre-auth token it also completes the login.
Starts registering a passkey or security key (session or pre-auth token in stage `enroll`).

get.summary: Download a blob (member with `view_channel` in the conversation).
My DMs and group DMs, most recent activity first.

post.summary: Start a DM (idempotent: an existing DM is returned with 200) or a group DM.

get.summary: My message requests: conversations of people who are not my friends, until I accept or decline them.
One DM or group DM (members only).

patch.summary: Rename a group DM (any member).

post.summary: Accept a message request: the conversation becomes a normal DM or group DM (idempotent).

get.summary: The conversation's call: running or not, who started it, who is connected and who is still ringing.

post.summary:
Decline a ringing call. In a DM the call ends (`system.call.missed`); in a group only this user stops
ringing.
Join (answer) a running call.
Leave the call (this device). The last one to leave ends it.

Start a call (or join the running one): rings every other member (`call.ring`, on other nodes through
their home node) and returns a LiveKit token. Unanswered calls end after 45 seconds as missed. At most
10 new calls per user and 10 minutes (`429`; development nodes 1000).

patch.summary: Change this device's own state in the call (mute, deafen, screen share, camera).

get.summary: The application commands the caller can invoke in this conversation right now (§5.4).

post.summary: Decline a message request: I leave the conversation (the sender is not told), optionally blocking them.

Send an ephemeral event to the conversation: fanned out over the WebSocket (`ephemeral`) to every
member with read access except the sending device, never stored. The node reads only the type and,
for `whiteboard.open`, `whiteboard.grant` and `whiteboard.close`, the plaintext `session` field; it
announces session changes as `whiteboard.session`. 30 events per second and sender.

get.summary:
Unacknowledged shares addressed to the requester (oldest first, at most 100): every format 1 share and the format 2
shares with a box for the requesting device, with only that box.

post.summary:
Share keys of past epochs with a member who joined later. Allowed in encrypted room channels under every policy
(under `since_join` for the epochs since the recipient's join: its window bounds what it is served and accepts),
from an attested device of a member to a member with `read_history`.

delete.summary: Acknowledge (and drop) a share addressed to the requester; the requester is no longer pending.

get.summary:
Members of the channel who still wait for history keys (at most 100, the last 30 days): also under `since_join`,
for the messages posted between a member's join and its device's first leaf. Empty for DMs, group DMs and
plaintext channels.

put.summary:
Publish the inbox key of an epoch of an encrypted channel with webhooks (ENCRYPTION.md §5b): sent by the device
that committed the epoch, by the creator of a webhook and by members whose node has no key yet.

post.summary: Invoke an application command (§5.5); waits at most 3 seconds for the application's first response.
Add a member to a group DM (any member; the new member must be allowed under the DM policy).

delete.summary:
Leave a group DM (own username) or, as its creator, remove a member. Remaining members get
`mls.remove_needed` for the leaves of the departed user.

get.summary: Messages of any conversation (channel, DM, group DM), newest first.

parameters.name: around
parameters.description:
The page around this message (jump to a search result): up to `limit / 2` newer messages, the message
itself and older ones, newest first. Not combinable with `before`, `after` or `epoch`; `404
message.not_found` if the message is not in this conversation or not visible to the caller.

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description:
Only encrypted messages of this MLS epoch (used to check shared history keys, ENCRYPTION.md §7b). Lists
the messages of the whole channel, threads included.

parameters.name: thread
parameters.description: Page this thread of the channel (PROTOCOL.md §7e); without it the channel's list leaves thread messages out.

parameters.name: threads
parameters.description: `all`: the channel's messages including those of its threads (clients syncing their local search index).

post.summary: Send a message to any conversation. DMs and group DMs only accept encrypted content.

delete.summary: Delete a message in any conversation (own messages; others' with `manage_messages`).

patch.summary: Edit an own message in any conversation.

put.summary: Add a reaction in any conversation.

delete.summary: Remove an own reaction in any conversation.

post.summary:
Submit a commit (§4.4). The first commit for an epoch wins; the node validates it and applies
the authorization rules of §4.5.

Create the conversation's MLS group (first wins). The GroupInfo must be for epoch 0 and
contain exactly the uploader's attested device.

get.summary: Latest GroupInfo for joining by external commit.
Handshake log in ascending epoch order.

parameters.name: since_epoch
parameters.description: First epoch to return (default 0).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 100 (default 100).

get.summary:
Leaves of the conversation's group that must be removed (ENCRYPTION.md §4.7): for members, so that a device
that was offline when `mls.remove_needed` went out still cleans up. Only leaves still in the group are listed.
Pinned messages of any conversation.

put.summary: Pin a message in any conversation.

delete.summary: Unpin a message in any conversation.

put.summary:
Mark a conversation read up to a message (members with `view_channel`; markers never move
backwards). The user's other connections get `read.update`.

get.summary:
The requester's upload categories in a conversation (room channels: roles and overrides; DMs: the
node's `TAVRN_UPLOAD_DM_CATEGORIES`).

post.summary: Upload an attachment to any conversation (see the room route).

get.summary:
The current whiteboard session of a conversation (null without one); changes arrive as
`whiteboard.session`.
Listed nodes (this node itself included while it allows listing), ordered by domain. Public, CORS-open.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1–100, default 100.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search in domain, name and description (at most 100 characters).

get.summary:
One listed node with the fingerprints of its keys as this node sees them (clients compare them with
their own fetch, §9.2). Public, CORS-open.

post.summary:
Reports another node or one of its rooms to this node's admins (FEDERATION.md §9.2): local users
only, 10 per user and 24 hours. Reports never block anything on their own; they show up in the
admin's Federation tab, and the third distinct reporter of a domain within 7 days leaves an admin
notice in the audit log (`directory.reports_notice`).

get.summary:
This node's discoverable rooms and the cached rooms of listed nodes, most members first. Public,
CORS-open; `local=true` returns only this node's own rooms (what other nodes fetch).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1–200, default 50.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search in name and description (at most 100 characters).

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: Only rooms of this node.

parameters.name: local
parameters.description: Only this node's own rooms.

parameters.name: min_members
parameters.description: Only rooms with at least this many members.

get.summary:
The image of any emoji of this node, room or personal, without authentication: content of
every conversation references emojis by id (`<:name:ID@host>`), and readers on every node load them from
here. Ids are random; nothing about rooms or owners is revealed. `?still=1`: the still variant.

parameters.name: still
parameters.description: `1`: the still variant (first frame) of an animated emoji.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The node hosting the emoji when it is not this one: this node serves its cached copy (fetched once).

200.description: WebP (or PNG/GIF/JPEG of emojis uploaded before conversion)

post.summary:
Throwaway conformance room for the probe of another node (FEDERATION.md §9.1): only a federated
session of a `tavrn-conformance` user, regardless of `TAVRN_ROOM_CREATION`, deleted after 15 minutes.

delete.summary: Deletes the probe's conformance room.

post.summary:
Server-to-server notifications (FEDERATION.md §5.1), authenticated with a node token. Body: the
envelope `{ id, type, from, to, at, payload }`, at most 64 KiB.

KeyPackage claim of another node on behalf of one of its users (FEDERATION.md §3.5), authenticated
with a node token. Body `{ user, requester }`: one KeyPackage per attested device of the local `user`.

get.summary:
The discovery document of another node as this node fetched and validated it (FEDERATION.md §1.4),
for web clients that cannot load `https://<domain>/.well-known/tavrn` themselves. Public; the node's
federation client applies its SSRF rules, the domain policy and the document cache.

State of a peer as this node sees it: conformance result, block state and key fingerprints. Public,
CORS-open, limited per client IP.

Resolves another node like this node does for its own requests (well-known, then the
`_tavrn._tcp.<domain>` SRV record, then `https://<domain>`) and returns its endpoints. Public, rate
limited per IP together with `/federation/peer/{domain}`.

post.summary: Federation token for one target node (FEDERATION.md §2.4). The home node does not contact the target.

get.summary: GIF search through the provider the node configured (Giphy or Tenor).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term; empty = trending

post.summary:
The application's first response to an interaction (app token with the `commands` scope): `reply`,
`defer` or `error`. Only the first response counts; after 3 seconds it is `410 interaction.expired`.
A follow-up of the application (until the interaction expires, at most 10).

get.summary: Preview of an invite (room name, rules), without joining.

post.summary: Join by invite.
Submit a takedown notice (no account needed; captcha when the node has one; 5 per hour and address).

get.summary:
The reporter's status page of a case (needs the token of the confirmation mail; unknown cases and wrong tokens
answer alike).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token of the confirmation mail.

get.summary: The published legal documents (public).
One published document (public).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: imprint | privacy | terms | cookies

get.summary:
A stored image (avatar, header, room icon) by its id; public. The id changes with every upload, so
responses are cached for a year.
The animated variant of a stored image (animated WebP).

Pending removals of the caller's own leaves on this node, in every conversation (ENCRYPTION.md §4.7): any device
of the user may remove them (own-user rule of §4.5), e.g. right after connecting.
Pending Welcomes for the session's device.

delete.summary: Delete a processed Welcome of the session's device.

get.summary: Public summary of the node for the client (sign-in page, header).

Presences of the users on this node I may see and who are not offline (friends, members of shared
rooms that do not hide their presence there, members of shared DMs). Everyone else is offline.
VAPID key for web push.
get.description:
Whether this node sends web pushes (`TAVRN_PUSH`) and the VAPID public key (RFC 8292) browsers subscribe with
(`applicationServerKey`). Public; `public_key` is null while push is off.

post.summary: Report a message, a user or a room.
post.description:
Any authenticated user (also users of other nodes with a session here), never bots. Room content goes to the
room's moderators and the node admins, everything else to the node admins (MODERATION.md §1.1). For messages of
encrypted conversations the reporter may release their plaintext as `evidence`; plaintext messages are linked and
snapshotted by the node. A report of the same target by the same reporter while the first is open is merged
(`200`). At most `TAVRN_REPORTS_RATE_PER_HOUR` reports per hour.

get.summary: One report with its evidence.
get.description:
For node admins, and for the room's moderators (`moderate_members`) when the report is about the room's content
and not about themselves. Everybody else gets `404 report.not_found`.

delete.summary: Delete a report and its evidence.
delete.description: Node admins only, at any time (audited as `report.delete`).

patch.summary: Change a report's status, assignee or resolution note.
patch.description:
Whoever may see the report. `status`: `open`, `resolved` or `dismissed`; `assignee_id`: a moderator who may see
the report, or null. Sends `report.update`.

post.summary: Act on a report: delete the message, time out, kick, ban or purge the reported user.
post.description:
Runs the existing moderation route on the report's target with the caller's permissions (same checks and errors)
and records the report id in that route's audit entry (`meta.report_id`) and the action in the report.

`{ mode?, muted_until? }` (`muted_until`: RFC 3339 or `"forever"`). At most 500 rooms, 2000 channels and
64 KiB. The user's other devices get `notifications.update`.

get.summary: List the own push subscriptions.

requesting device. Keys and endpoints are not returned, only the push service's origin.

put.summary: Register a push subscription.
put.description:
Registers the browser's push subscription (`PushSubscription.toJSON()`) for the requesting device, or updates
the account's one with the same endpoint (also from another of its devices). `201` when new, `200` when
updated. An endpoint of another account's live subscription is refused (`409 push.endpoint_taken`: the client
unsubscribes the browser and subscribes again); a stale one (expired, or its device has no live session) is
taken over. The endpoint must be an `https://` URL of a public host (`400
push.endpoint_invalid`), `keys.p256dh` an uncompressed P-256 point and `keys.auth` 16 bytes, both base64url
(`400 push.keys_invalid`). At most 20 subscriptions per account (`409 push.too_many`), 30 registrations per
hour (`429`). `404 push.disabled` while push is off. The subscription is deleted with the device and when its
sessions are revoked (sign-out).

post.description:
Queues a push of type `test` to every deliverable subscription of the account, even while a device is connected
(the settings' test button). `202`; at most 5 per 10 minutes (`429`), `404 push.disabled` while push is off.

delete.summary: Delete a push subscription.
delete.description:
Deletes one push subscription of the account (any of its devices). Clients call it when the user turns push off
on a device and before signing out. `404 push.subscription_not_found` otherwise.

(`name@other.node`, only users this node knows; the mirror is refreshed in the background when stale).

node (`alice@other.example`) this node claims them from the user's home node and returns the ones

knows (`alice@other.example`), the answer comes from its key cache, i.e. the view of the user's home

post.summary:
A throwaway LiveKit room for the connection test of the voice settings (VOICE.md §10.4): the client
connects with chosen candidate types (UDP per address, TCP, TURN) and reports which work. The token can
only join that empty room, hidden and without publishing; LiveKit drops the room a minute after use.

LiveKit webhooks (`Authorization`: a JWT signed with the node's LiveKit secret, carrying the SHA-256 of
the body). Only LiveKit (on the same host) knows the secret.

Post a message through a webhook (no authentication: the secret is part of the URL). Unknown ids and wrong
secrets both answer `404 webhook.not_found`. In encrypted channels: a `SealedPayload` for webhooks sealed by the
sender (`400 webhook.sealed_required` otherwise), the plaintext payload for webhooks sealed by the node;
`409 webhook.pending_key` until a member has published the channel's inbox key.

Is the process alive? Always answers 200 while the server runs; reports the state of LiveKit.

Can the node serve requests? Checks the database, with voice whether LiveKit answers, and with
`TAVRN_CACHE_URL` the shared cache.

binary values base64url), for `PublicKeyCredential.parse…OptionsFromJSON`.

id.description: base64url WebAuthn credential id (also used in paths).

prf_supported.description: The credential supports the PRF extension (can unlock the secret storage).

WebauthnInfo.description:
The WebAuthn relying party id (`TAVRN_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID`, default the identity domain). It may be a parent
domain of the web client's host (delegation); clients pass it as `rpId` on assertions they build
themselves (the secret storage PRF, PROTOCOL.md §5a.4).

oneOf.description:
Passkey-only login: continue an existing device of the account (PROTOCOL.md §5b); ignored for the second
factor (the password step carries it).

device_name.description: Name of the new device (passkey-only login; otherwise taken from the login).

preauth_token.description: Required for the second-factor ceremony (the one started with it).

With a pre-auth token (stage `verify`): second factor, allow-list of the user's
credentials. Without: passkey-only login with a discoverable credential.

name.description: Shown in the list, 1–64 characters.

recovery_codes.description: Ten single-use codes when this is the account's first factor.

oneOf.description: The session, when registered with a pre-auth token (stage `enroll`).

Webhook.description: A webhook as shown to holders of `manage_webhooks` (never its secret).

allow_mentions_everyone.description: Executions may set `mentions_everyone` (only a creator holding `mention_everyone` can allow it).

avatar.description: Path of the avatar on this node (animated variant if any), null without one.

created_by.description: Address of the creator (null if unknown).

pending_key.description:
Sealed, but no member has published the channel's inbox key yet: executions answer
`409 webhook.pending_key`.

sealing.description:
Encrypted channels: `sender` (the service seals) or `node` (the node seals what it receives); null in
unencrypted channels (APPLICATIONS.md §6.1a).

suspended.description: Always false since webhooks post into encrypted channels as well (kept for compatibility).

user.description: The pseudo user that authors the webhook's messages (`kind = "webhook"`).

WebhookPayload.description: The execution payload (§6.1). Unknown fields (for example `attachments`) are refused.

content.description: A plaintext `text` content object (PROTOCOL.md §7), optionally with `embeds` (§6.4).

mentions.description: Addresses to mention; addresses that are not members of the room are dropped.

reply_to.description: A message of the same channel this one replies to.

thread_id.description: A thread of the channel to post into; required in forum channels (a post), which show no loose messages.

username.description: Name shown for this message instead of the webhook's name.

WebhookRef.description: The node-set envelope field of a webhook message (APPLICATIONS.md §6.1).

name.description: The per-message `username` or the webhook's name when the message was posted.

age.description: Date of birth and age gates (`age.v1`, PROTOCOL.md §5e).

api.description: API base of the node (`<TAVRN_PUBLIC_URL>/api/v1`); its host may differ from `domain` (delegation).

oneOf.description: Present while federation is enabled (FEDERATION.md §1.1).

web.description:
Origin of this node's web client (FEDERATION.md §8: the connect flow redirects to
`<web>/connect`); `TAVRN_WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN`, default the public URL.

webauthn.description: WebAuthn relying party of this node's passkeys (PROTOCOL.md §5a.4).

WhiteboardSession.description: The whiteboard session of a conversation as the node knows it.

device_id.description: The owner's device presenting the board (the device id other clients know).

open_for_all.description: Everyone who can view the conversation may edit.

owner.description: Address of the owner (the user who opened the board).

owner_id.description: Node-local user id of the owner.
